captions.instagram:
How does a piano work?

Press a key and a chain of levers flings a felt hammer at steel strings pulling with nearly 20 tonnes. Take a grand piano apart in 3D, slow the hammer down 50 times, and play it yourself.

→ A grand piano is 88 keys, 88 hammers, about 230 strings and a big wooden soundboard.
→ Its strings pull with nearly 20 tonnes, so a cast-iron plate holds them tight.
→ Press a key and a chain of levers flings a felt hammer up at the string.
→ Just before it hits, the jack slips away, so the hammer flies free and bounces off.
→ A struck string vibrates as a whole, and in halves, thirds and quarters at the same time.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/pianoclear (link in bio)

Box No. 006 of 365. Follow @glassbox.how for a new "how it works" every day.

youtubeLong.title: How does a piano work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Press a key and a chain of levers flings a felt hammer at steel strings pulling with nearly 20 tonnes. Take a grand piano apart in 3D, slow the hammer down 50 times, and play it yourself.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/pianoclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/pianoclear

In this video:
• Hammers, strings and a wooden board. A piano is a string instrument played with hammers.
• A chain of levers that lets go. The key lifts a lever called the wippen, which pushes the hammer up through a jack.
• Length, tension and weight set the note. A string's frequency is f = (1/2L)·√(T/μ): halve the length for one octave up, or pull four times as hard.
• The soundboard makes it loud. A string is too thin to push much air, so on its own it is nearly silent.
• 88 keys, each 1.0595 times the last. From A0 at 27.5 Hz to C8 at 4,186 Hz, with A4 tuned to 440 Hz.
• Soft, loud, and three pedals. Press faster and the hammer flies faster: louder, and brighter because the felt touches the string for less time.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
